correctness.rationale: Ranking independent chord endpoints generates each perfect matching with the same multiplicity. The crossing counts within disjoint groups are independent and their sum is pointwise bounded by the full count. On isolation the two arcs have independent uniform submatchings. Their crossing-count sum is bounded by the (n−1)-chord law, itself strictly smaller in increasing-test expectation because the extra chord crosses a specified existing chord with probability 1/3. Summing positive isolation-event weights gives the result, including n=2 and empty arcs. This is size bias, not conditioning on I_n>0. The replacement checker ran successfully for every designated pair and every relevant threshold at n=2..6 (python /workspace/repairs/2/verify.py); it is finite corroboration. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed.
